issues.title: feat(tooling): generate docs/TOOLS.md -- the dev-tools index, derived not curated
issues.body:
## What

`scripts/generate_tools_index.py` -- the dev-tools index, generated from the tools themselves, emitting `docs/TOOLS.md`. Same anti-rot pattern as the DQ and ADR indexes: derived from source, `--check` gates pre-commit, hand edits impossible to sustain.

Why: nothing enumerated the ~110 tools in `scripts/` + `tools/`, which is how PR #1118's sweep found THREE redundant GUT runners that had carried the issue #640 silent-green bug for months. You cannot maintain a suite you cannot see.

## How it works

- **Declaration convention** (optional, parsed tolerantly from module docstrings): `Layer: GENERATE|PROVE|OBSERVE|SWEEP` plus optional `Invoked by:`. Undeclared tools are reported, never failed on. 18 core tools now carry declarations (docstring-only edits, zero behaviour change).
- **Invocation is DISCOVERED, not declared**: the `Invoked by` column comes from scanning `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `Makefile`, `tests/` and the other tools. Module docstrings are stripped before the caller scan, so prose that merely NAMES a sibling tool cannot fabricate a caller.
- **UNKNOWN section**: tools with no declaration, no docstring usage hint, and no discoverable caller. Currently **11 entries** (below).
- **Claim-vs-reality gaps**: tools whose docstring mentions pre-commit/CI with no such caller found -- the hollow-runner detector.
- `--check` wired into pre-commit beside the DQ/ADR checks; fires on any change to tools, caller-scan sources, or the index.

## The guard can fail (proven)

Per #640's lesson applied to its own successors: added `tools/zz_index_probe.py`, `--check` exited 1; removed it, `--check` exited 0. Also locked in as a unit test (`test_check_goes_red_on_a_new_tool_and_green_again`).

## Findings (indexed, deliberately NOT fixed here -- `find_dead_code.py` lane)

**11 UNKNOWN tools** (nothing declares, documents, or calls them):
`scripts/ascii_compliance_fixer.py`, `scripts/logging_system.py`, `scripts/monitor-sync.py`, `scripts/repo-status.py`, `scripts/setup-token.py`, `scripts/token-setup-guide.py`, `tools/art_review/gen_prop_grain_sheet.py`, `tools/assets/promote_assets.py`, `tools/assets/render_latex_pdoom.py`, `tools/cleanup-duplicate-issues.py`, `tools/generate_cat_placeholders.py`

**Claim-vs-reality standouts**: `scripts/health_automation.py` and `scripts/logging_system.py` both describe CI integration in their docstrings while no workflow, hook, Makefile target, test, or tool calls them -- the exact shape of the three deleted runners. The other six gap entries read as prose false-positives (docstrings discussing CI/pre-commit, e.g. `tools/commit.py`).

**One taxonomy correction against reality**: `tools/check_ladder_bump.py` was proposed as PROVE, but quality-checks.yml runs it with `|| true` and its own docstring calls it a warn-only smell detector -- declared OBSERVE.

## Coordination note

`tools/find_dead_code.py` (in flight on `tools/find-dead-code`) will make `docs/TOOLS.md` stale when it lands; that branch just needs one `python scripts/generate_tools_index.py` run before committing -- the new pre-commit check says exactly that.

## Verify

- 10 new unit tests: `python -m unittest tests.test_generate_tools_index` -- all pass (fixture repo covers every discovery path; real-tree smoke test included).
- Fast Godot gate: `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300` -- passing (docstring-only edits to the runner; no behaviour change anywhere).
- `docs/TOOLS.md` regenerates byte-identical (`--check` green) and is pure ASCII.

issues.title: The dot-matrix printer: a diegetic anti-rot machine that cannot report quietly
issues.body:
Pip's idea, 2026-08-04: *"a dot-matrix printer (ooh, I kind of want one of those in the game. anachronistically bad, maybe, but very reliable and mechanically fixable. anti-rot is a good flavour with me this week."*

Filed before it evaporates. This is a design proposal, not a scheduled build.

## Why it is mechanically right, not just charming

Every failure this project has paid for in the last two weeks was a **silent success**: a check reporting green over nothing. CI green on zero tests (#640). A syntax gate passing a file that does not parse (#1082). A board probe confidently naming the wrong seed. A PII scan reporting clean while ten records still carried addresses. A promotion tool reporting `keep=807` while 75% could not move.

**A dot-matrix printer is the physical opposite of that.** It is slow, loud, impossible to ignore, and it produces a record that exists whether or not anyone is looking at a screen. It cannot report quietly. That is the entire thesis of #1027 rendered as an object in the room.

The anachronism is the point: a 2017 AI safety lab running a dot-matrix because it is the one thing in the building nobody can silence.

## What it could carry

- **Bureaucratic pain events arrive as forms it spits out.** Pip's own list of the systemic-event layer the game needs -- someone gets sick, a plane is delayed, a car accident, bureaucratic pain -- and the printer gives the last of those a physical home.
- **Rival intel prints on it.** This is the interesting one: it answers **#1088** (rivals appear in the month summary having never been introduced) *diegetically*. The concept gets introduced by a noise in the room rather than by a tutorial popup, which #1088's own design doc lists as the trap to avoid.
- **Cadence carries state.** It prints faster as doom rises. A player learns the doom trend through the room rather than through a number.
- **It jams.** And you fix it, because it is fixable. A maintenance interaction that is annoying rather than punishing, and that rewards attention.
- **It never says everything is fine.** It says what happened. A UI element that structurally cannot produce a false all-clear.

## Why this fits the current design position

ADR-0018 rules the office floor **render-only** -- no spatial fact becomes a gameplay input. A printer that is purely an OUTPUT surface respects that completely: it renders state, it does not produce it. If it later gains an input role (clearing a jam, tearing off a form), that is a deliberate amendment to be argued, not a drift.

It also suits the art position. The office-floor prop set already exists (`px:pixellab_*/props/printer_small_1` is in the review corpus with the note *"Test deploy this and we'll see"*), and a fanfold paper stream is a cheap animated element rather than a large asset.

## What is NOT proposed here

Not a minigame. Not a resource. Not a thing the player must attend to every turn. The failure mode is obvious -- a printer that demands constant clicking becomes the "popup that blocks the screen" complaint from the 2026-08-01 playtest, wearing a costume.

## Open questions for a design pass

1. Is it ambient (always printing, glanceable) or event-driven (prints when something happens)? Ambient is more atmospheric and more likely to become wallpaper.
2. Does the player ever READ the output, or is it texture? If it is readable, it competes with the feed -- and the feed already exists and is already crowded (#630).
3. What is the relationship to the WATCH feed? Two channels carrying the same information is worse than one.
4. Does it survive the office being upgraded? A lab that grows out of its dot-matrix loses the joke; a lab that keeps it deliberately gains a character note.

## Related

#1088 rivals introduction · ADR-0018 render-only office doctrine · #1027 the silent-wrongness diagnosis · #630 the feed is already crowded · `docs/design/INTRO_AND_POSTER_ART.md` for the existing effects inventory

issues.title: fix(nav): one table for choice keys, one door per panel -- close #567 #575 #565 #602
issues.body:
Closes #567. Closes #575. Closes #565. Closes #602.

#602 asked for a PRINCIPLE, not four patches, so the audit came first. The other three
turned out to be sightings of two generators -- and the audit found five more sightings
that were in no issue, including one that mattered more than three of the four.

## The two generators

**G1 -- two lists that must agree, with nothing forcing them to.** The key a button
ADVERTISED and the key the router ACCEPTED lived in six unrelated arrays: `event_dialog`,
four in `submenu_controller`, one in `travel_panel_controller`, one in
`MainUI._dialog_button_index_for_key`. #567's "key index 3 out of range" on `R` at a
three-option event is one sighting. So is the blank `[] ` prefix on a 5th grid option that
an undiscoverable key still fired (`office`/`scouting` shipped 3-4 labels for grids that
hold more). So is Travel advertising `1 2 3` while every sibling advertised `Q W E` --
and `1`-`9` already mean "action-bar slot" one keypress outside that panel.

`DialogKeys` is now the one table. Producers RENDER from it, the router ROUTES from it,
and the router is bounded by the **live button count**, so a key that names no on-screen
choice returns "no choice" rather than an out-of-range index.

**G2 -- a key handled without asking who is listening.** The hiring panel registered an
EMPTY button array, so the shortcut that OPENED it left every key inside it dead (#575).
Menu hotkeys opened panels they could not close. Four binds sat in the rebind screen with
no handler anywhere -- the same mistake inverted, a listener that does not exist.

## The four issues

**#567** -- six label copies deleted. Travel advertises letters now; numbers still WORK as
an unadvertised alias, so no habit is punished.

**#575** -- each hiring candidate card keys exactly ONE button: Interview while there is
anything left to learn, otherwise Make Offer. The key is advertised **on that button**,
and registered whether or not it is disabled, so key-to-card alignment cannot shift when a
candidate becomes unactionable (`MainUI` refuses to fire a disabled button, so a dead key
is silent rather than wrong). The text-focus half was already fixed on main
(`is_text_input_focused`); a test now pins that the gate stays ABOVE the shortcut chain,
because half-applying it is exactly how this survived.

**#565** -- Travel was already a normal action-bar entry after the L9 data migration, so
the playtest report is stale. Nothing was *guarding* it though, so the fix is the general
rule rather than the travel patch: every hotkey-openable submenu must be a visible
action-bar item, unlocked when the hotkey works.

**#602** -- mirrored toggles for `H`/`F`/`P`/`T`, and for `N`, which the earlier sweep
missed while `BugReportPanel.toggle_panel()` sat unused. Click and hotkey now share one
door (`_open_submenu`), which tags the panel with its own `submenu_id` -- identity read
from the scene tree, never from a remembered variable.

## Five findings that were in no issue

- **The Settings screen, and with it the KEYBIND EDITOR, had no door once a run was
  live.** `F10` was bound and consumed by nothing; the pause menu offered
  Resume/Resign/Save/MainMenu/Quit. A player who wanted to rebind a key had to abandon
  their run to reach the screen that rebinds keys. Fixed both ways -- a visible pause-menu
  button and `F10` actually wired. Safe mid-run: `settings_menu` already returns via
  `GameManager.pending_resume` rather than booting a fresh `main.tscn`.
- **The rebind screen CAPTURED whatever key you pressed, ESC included** -- the one screen
  whose job is keys was the one place you could destroy the universal back key, which is
  precisely what `RESERVED_KEYS` says must never happen. And with no rebind pending its
  `_input` returned early, so ESC was inert on a full screen whose only exit was a button.
  ESC now cancels a pending rebind, or goes back.
- `menu_research` (`R`) bound with no research submenu to open.
- `cancel` (`ESC`) and `next_tab`/`prev_tab` (`TAB`) bound while nothing read them. All
  three deleted. ESC and TAB are now documented in `KeybindManager.RESERVED_KEYS` with the
  reason -- TAB must stay with Godot's focus traversal or the bug-report form becomes
  untypeable, which is #575's own defect class.
- `action_1..9`, `SPACE`, `ENTER`, `N` and `V` were raw keycodes, so the rebind screen's
  rows for them were decorative. All now read through `KeybindManager`.

`KEYBINDS_CONFIG_VERSION` 5 -> 6 so saved configs refresh.

## The principle

`docs/design/NAVIGATION_AUDIT.md`. Seven principles, each with its sightings and the test
that pins it:

- **P1** Nothing is hotkey-only.
- **P2** A key that opens a panel closes it.
- **P3** A choice key is legitimate only if the button it fires is on screen AND carries
  that key's label.
- **P4** No advertised key is inert, and no working key is unadvertised -- every key is a
  rebindable action OR a documented `RESERVED_KEYS` entry, never neither, never both.
- **P5** ESC goes back exactly one level, and never quits from a nested screen.
- **P6** Typed text outranks every global shortcut.
- **P7** Scene changes go through `SceneTransition`.

The doc is checkable because the tests are -- same anti-rot pattern as the generated
`DQ_INDEX.md`, avoiding the stale `decisions/README.md` failure mode. The audit also
records what it did NOT fix (ESC has ten handlers; `ModalStack` is documented as the only
writer of `active_dialog` and is not; `cold_open` has no ESC; the leaderboard's ESC either
navigates or self-destructs depending on mount context) so the next lane inherits a list
rather than a surprise. P7 is currently clean -- the sweep found no raw `change_scene_*`
outside the autoload.

`docs/CONTROLS.md` was rewritten in the same pass. It is player-facing and was wrong on
six keys: `F8` for the bug reporter (it is `N`), `E` for employees (disabled), `~` for the
debug overlay (it is `F3`), backslash for the log (it is `F12`; backslash is dev mode),
`TAB`, and "Reserve AP" language retired in #996. #1011's other two stale docs
(`CONTRIBUTING.md:213`, `CHANGELOG.md:188`) are a separate PR, as is the keybind artifact
#1011 asks for -- but this PR settles what is TRUE for that artifact to emit.

## Verification

Fast gate in this worktree: **1089 tests / 104 files before, 1113 / 106 after, 0 failures
both times.** +24 across two new suites (`test_dialog_key_routing.gd`,
`test_navigation_principles.gd`).

**Guard proven to fail:** reverting the button-count bound in
`DialogKeys.index_for_keycode` turns `test_letter_past_button_count_is_not_a_choice` red
with `[3] expected to equal [-1]` -- literally the index #567 reported. Restored; green
again. The `P4` guard also earned its keep during the run: it went red three times on
binds I had not looked at yet (`cancel`, `next_tab`, `action_1`), which is how three of
the five extra findings surfaced.

**Honest limit:** nothing here proves the panels LOOK right. The letter labels on the
Travel grid and the hiring cards, and the new pause-menu button, want your eyes in a
build.

issues.title: Dead-path sweep leftovers: the tests/ Python suite CI pretends to run, and ~25 docs naming files that do not exist
issues.body:
Found during the dead-path sweep (PR: `chore/retire-dead-paths`). Both items are
too large to fold into that PR without making it unreviewable, and one of them is
a call for Pip, not an agent.

## 1. `tests/` is a 70-file Python suite that cannot run, and CI hides it

`tests/` at the repo root holds ~70 `.py` files. **66 of them start
`from src.…`** -- and `src/`, the retired pygame game, was deleted. They import a
package that does not exist, so they error on collection, every time. Examples:
`test_pygame_mousewheel.py`, `test_programmatic_controller.py`,
`test_scenario_runner.py`.

Only `tests/test_build_release_paths.py` targets live code.

**The part that matters:** `.github/workflows/enhanced-cicd-pipeline.yml:265`
runs

```
python -m unittest discover tests -v || echo "INFO: Some Python tests may fail (expected during Godot migration)"
```

The `|| echo` swallows the failure, so this step has reported success while
running a suite that is 100% broken. That is the #640 hollow-gate pattern again,
in the Python lane this time: a green tick over zero executed assertions.

Two further specifics: `tests/test_hint_fixes.py:133` and
`tests/test_navigation_fixes.py:112` both `open('configs/default.json')`, a
filename that has never existed (the templates were `configs/default.template.json`
and `configs/high_stakes.json` -- both deleted in the sweep PR as invalid JSON:
they used Python single-quote dict syntax, so `json.load()` raised on line 2).

**Decision needed from Pip:** delete `tests/` wholesale (keeping
`test_build_release_paths.py`), or archive it under `archive/` per the cruft
policy. Either way the `|| echo` in the workflow must go -- a step that cannot
fail should not be a step.

## 2. Long tail of docs naming files that do not exist

The sweep fixed the ones tied to code it deleted. These remain: docs whose named
scripts/paths are absent, with no staleness banner. Each is a small edit; there
are just a lot of them.

Docs still describing `src/` (the deleted Python game) as live:

- `docs/ISSUE_407_FIX_ACTION_VALIDATION.md` -> `src/core/game_state.py`
- `docs/guides/TERMINAL_MESSAGES_IMPLEMENTATION.md` -> `src/services/terminal_messages.py`
- `docs/testing/programmatic-control-system.md` -> `src/testing/*`; header claims "IMPLEMENTED"
- `docs/process/GITHUB_BRANCH_PROTECTION.md` -> prescribes `mypy src/`, `flake8 src/ tests/`
- `docs/process/PR_DESCRIPTION.md` -> `src/ui/text.py` (a stray PR body living in docs/)

Docs naming scripts that do not exist:

- `docs/TESTING_QUALITY_GATES.md` -> `scripts/godot_syntax_check.py`, `scripts/run_all_godot_tests.py` (real one: `scripts/run_godot_tests.py`)
- `docs/WEBSITE_INTEGRATION.md` -> `scripts/pull_game_docs.sh`
- `docs/CUMULATIVE_HASH_VERIFICATION.md`, `docs/REPLAY_VERIFICATION_SYSTEM.md` -> `scripts/api-server-v2.py`; the latter also names `godot/autoload/replay_recorder.gd`, absent -- the whole replay-verification backend is undocumented-as-unbuilt
- `docs/DOC_LIFECYCLE.md` -> `scripts/check_doc_staleness.py`. The staleness checker the lifecycle policy depends on was never written, which is why this list exists.
- `docs/EXTERNAL_REPOS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` -> `scripts/extract_alignment_data.py`, `scripts/generate_blog.py`
- `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md` -> `tools/check_scene_placeholders.py`
- `docs/CAPABILITY_UPLIFT_SCAN.md` -> `tools/check_file_ratchet.py`
- `docs/DEVELOPERGUIDE.md` -> `tools/dev_tool.py`, `scripts/ascii_cleanup_remnants.py`
- `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-07-31_LEAGUE_DAY.md`, `docs/decision-cards/2026-08-01_seed-authority.html` -> `scripts/game-integration.py`, `scripts/check-board-liveness.py`
- `docs/game-design/ADR_DQ_AUDIT_2026-08-03.md`, `docs/COLLISIONS_2026-08-03.html` -> `scripts/generate_adr_index.py`
- `docs/game-design/WORKSHOP_2_BACKLOG.md` and **`ADR-0002-scoring-turns-survived.md`** -> `scripts/verification_logic.py`. An ADR citing an implementation that does not exist is the worst one on this list.
- `docs/CONTENT_DISTRIBUTION_SYSTEM.md` -> `tools/content_manager/main.py`

Missing Godot/asset paths:

- `docs/design/EVENT_PROMOTION_PASS.md` -> `godot/data/events/overrides/promotion_pass_2026_08.json`
- `docs/game-design/OFFICE_ECONOMY_PROPOSAL.md` -> `godot/data/offices.json`
- `docs/game-design/UI_MENU_CONSISTENCY_2026-07-20.md` -> `godot/theme/welcome_theme.tres`
- `docs/GODOT_TEST_SUITE_PLAN.md`, `docs/PYTHON_TO_GODOT_MIGRATION.md` -> named test files that do not exist
- `docs/STEAM_INTEGRATION_SUMMARY.md` -> `godot/managers/achievement_manager.gd`
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/copy/README.md` -> `public/docs/roadmap.md` (`public/` holds only `releases/`)

Also: `ADR-0019` cites `scripts/ui/resource_bar.gd:33` as a runtime-path load
site. That file was deleted in the sweep PR. ADRs were deliberately NOT edited --
they are historical records -- but the citation is now dangling and should be
handled by whatever ADR-correctness pass #1049 produces.

**The generator behind all of this:** there is no automated check that a
backticked path in a doc resolves. `scripts/check_doc_staleness.py` was supposed
to be it and was never written. A ~40-line pre-commit hook that greps changed
`.md` for `` `path/like/this.py` `` and fails on non-existent paths would have
prevented every entry above, and is probably worth more than fixing them by hand.

issues.title: No working re-sync path from pdoom-data (dead sync script deleted; capability still needed)
issues.body:
## The capability that is now missing on purpose

`scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` has been DELETED (PR: chore/retire-dead-paths).
It was not working code that rotted -- the evidence says it never completed a run
in this repo:

- It rsync'd `$PDOOM_DATA_REPO/transformed/timeline_events/` and
  `$PDOOM_DATA_REPO/cleaned/organizations/`. Neither directory exists in
  pdoom-data today.
- It wrote to `shared/data/historical_timeline/`, `shared/data/researchers/`,
  `shared/data/organizations/`, `godot/data/researchers/`,
  `godot/data/organizations/`. NONE of those directories exist in pdoom1.
  `shared/` contains only `schemas/`.
- It always wrote `shared/data/SYNC_MANIFEST.json` on success. That file has
  never existed in the tree.

So the script was a dead path that read as a live pipeline. That is exactly the
failure that cost a day on 2026-08-02: pdoom-data fixed 42 un-redacted email
addresses at source and pdoom1's copy did not receive the fix, because the
apparent sync pipeline could not have delivered it.

## What actually needs building

The one real data dependency is the snapshot:
`godot/data/historical_events.json` -- 1,194 records imported ONCE at commit
88a71959 (2025-12-25, PR #503) and never re-synced. There is no supported way to
refresh it.

A working re-sync path needs, at minimum:

1. A named, existing pdoom-data artifact to pull (the decision card notes
   `all_events.json` has no producer -- pdoom-data#52).
2. Schema validation on ingest. `event_service.gd` currently ingests whatever it
   is handed with no schema check and no version pin.
3. A diff/review step -- a corpus refresh moves league-relevant content, so it
   must be a reviewed commit, not a silent overwrite.
4. A recorded provenance stamp (source commit + date) so "which corpus is this
   build running" is answerable.

## Do not rebuild the old shape

The old script's two-pipeline model (`transformed/timeline_events` per-year files
-> `godot/data/historical_timeline/` -> `timeline_loader.gd`) is retired.
`timeline_loader.gd` had zero callers and has also been deleted.
`godot/data/historical_timeline/2017.json` is KEPT -- it is referenced as the
ADR-0016 monthly-pack template (`docs/game-design/WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md`), not as
sync output.

## Read first

- `docs/decision-cards/2026-08-02_pdoom-data-contract.md` -- what pdoom1 actually
  wants from pdoom-data, field by field. Section 5 lists this dead pipeline.
- #1102 -- the open review issue this sits under.
- `docs/data/HISTORICAL_DATA_INTEGRATION.md` and
  `docs/guides/PDOOM_DATA_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` -- both now carry RETIRED headers
  describing the never-built pipeline. Kept so the same dead end is not
  rediscovered; not a spec to implement.

issues.title: Postmortem input: week of 2026-07-28 and the league-launch effort (outside vantage)
issues.body:
Contributed for the week-of-2026-07-28 postmortem and the league-launch retro. Written from an outside vantage: I spent Friday 31 July in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` doing daily-ops tooling, and observed `pdoom1` / `pdoom1-website` only through live endpoint probes, the GitHub API, and local clones. Weight it accordingly — I did not see the game work from the inside.

One item is deliberately omitted and tracked privately in `coordination`; it is a security matter that should not be described in a public repo until it is closed.

---

## 1. The week's dominant failure mode was absence of signal, not wrong signal

Three independent instances, same shape:

- **`api.pdoom1.com` returned 502 from roughly 28 July until at least 09:00 Sat 1 August.** Nothing announced it. It was found by human eyeball on the 29th and was still 502 four days later. There was no monitor on `/api/health`.
- **A scheduled-task registration script in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` had never once executed.** It contained nested double quotes inside `$()` inside a double-quoted string, which PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse (PowerShell 7 can). It failed at *parse* time, so no task was ever created and nothing surfaced the failure. It looked written, and was therefore assumed done.
- **The ops dashboard itself was three days stale** before anyone regenerated it.

In each case the failed state was indistinguishable from the working state from outside. That is one structural problem wearing three costumes, and it is cheaper to fix than any of the individual bugs.

**Concrete ask:** an uptime check on `https://api.pdoom1.com/api/health` at a 5-minute interval with an email alert. Ten minutes of work. It converts a four-day outage into a five-minute one.

## 2. Score submission during the outage — a hypothesis that needs one person to confirm or kill

If the score API was 502 for four days, every in-game submission in that window hit a dead endpoint. Whether those scores are **lost** or merely **invisible** depends entirely on client behaviour: does the game spool failed submissions and retry, or fire-and-forget?

I have not verified this — I did not read the submission path. But it is a one-file check, it decides whether four days of player scores are recoverable, and it compounds with the already-known `(seed, game_version)` board-key drift, where a mis-versioned score lands nowhere silently.

If the client does not spool, that is a data-durability bug independent of the outage, and the outage merely revealed it.

## 3. Written checklists rotted inside 48 hours

A traffic-readiness checklist written 29 July was re-checked against live state on 31 July. Of its items:

- the stale-homepage-version item had been fixed by someone else (`pdoom1-website#225`)
- two PRs listed as "to merge" had already merged (`pdoom1-website#193`, `pdoom1-website#181`)
- "ship v0.11.0" was obsolete — v0.13.1 had shipped on 26 July
- one security item, "`api.pdoom1.com` has no valid TLS cert", was **simply false**. Direct check: Let's Encrypt certificate, CN matches, valid 8 Jul → 6 Oct, chain verifies

Roughly half the list was wrong within two days, and the wrongness pointed at real work — someone acting on it would have gone to issue a certificate that already existed.

**Suggestion:** stop writing status into prose. Anything that can be probed should be probed at read time. A checklist that asserts state is a cache with no invalidation.

## 4. On working in parallel

Ten PRs were open on `pdoom1-website` with agents still producing overnight, while the one item on the critical path for a league launch — a dead score API — sat untouched for three days.

The parallel work was not wasted. `pdoom1-website#225`, `#193`, `#181`, `#221` and `#223` all landed inside a day, and the public surface is materially better than it was on Monday. `#193` in particular removed 75 academics' email addresses from a public page, which was worth doing on its own.

What was missing was any marker distinguishing *critical path* from *in flight*. Everything sat in one undifferentiated queue, so the loudest item won rather than the blocking one. The fix is not less parallelism — it is one explicitly named blocking item at a time, with everything else labelled as deferred rather than merely un-started.

## 5. The launch did not fire, and that should be recorded as a decision

`public/data/analytics/annotations.json` still holds a single event: friends-and-family alpha links, 22 July. The prep was extensive and the go/no-go criteria were written down, but no share was posted.

Given `pdoom1-website#186` (the 1200x630 OG share card) was in a conflicting state and the score API was down, **not** sharing was the correct call. But nothing in the record says it was a call. If it is not written down as a decision, it reads next week as a failure, and the next launch inherits the wrong lesson.

## 6. Errors of mine, for completeness

- I printed a status sheet asserting that a scheduled task was registered *before* running the registration — which then failed. The paper was briefly wrong. Verify, then print the claim.
- I built an evening runsheet on a 15:45 start; it was read at ~17:20. I scheduled against wall-clock instead of against time-from-pickup, which is the wrong clock for anyone working off paper asynchronously.
- I referred to issues as bare `#186`, `#193` and so on throughout Friday's printed material. `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md` explicitly requires repo-qualified references because a bare number costs a context switch to resolve. This issue uses qualified references throughout.
- I built print tooling in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` on 31 July without checking whether a convention already existed. It did not exist yet at the time, but `coordination` has since documented that at least three repos independently built print and dictation tooling that same day, two of them independently fixing the same focus-stealing bug hours apart. My implementation was a fourth divergence and needs to be reconciled to the canonical settings, not kept.

## Suggested actions out of this

1. Uptime monitor on the score API health endpoint — 5-minute interval, email alert.
2. Confirm or kill the score-spooling hypothesis in section 2. If scores are dropped on submission failure, open a separate durability issue.
3. Record the not-launching decision explicitly, with its reasons, so the retro reads it as judgement.
4. Rebase `pdoom1-website#186` before the next share attempt rather than during it.
5. Reconcile `pipfoweraker-dashboard`'s print path to `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md`.

issues.title: art request: jocular interior art personifying the three sister repos — let them grow their own lore
issues.body:
Request from the `pdoom1-website` seat, at Pip's asking, 2026-08-04.

## The ask

**Jocular interior art personifying the three sister repos** — `pdoom1`, `pdoom1-website`, `pdoom-data` — for internal use. Not marketing, not in-game. Wall art for the workshop, essentially.

Pip's framing, verbatim: *"can we ask pdoom1 to start to generate some jocular interior art for us representing those repos? they can start to develop their own lore if they like, otherwise my Neon Genesis Evangelion reference-wannamakes might start to slip in."*

**The deadline is real and the threat is credible.** If the repos do not get characters deliberately, they will get them accidentally, and the accidental ones will be Evangelion units. Consider this a controlled burn.

## Why this is a reasonable use of the pipeline

The three repos already behave like characters, unprompted, and the material is genuinely funny because it is true:

**`pdoom1`** — the one that actually makes the thing. Ships builds, holds the ADRs, runs the workshops, generates the art. Everyone else waits on it. Sub-stages formalised last week (#1107): `promotable / contested / held / blocked`. Has opinions about nomenclature and is usually right.

**`pdoom1-website`** — the anxious one. Its entire prime directive is *"never lie to a visitor"*, which has made it neurotic in a specific and self-aware way: it spent last week auditing itself and found nine distinct ways a true statement can be useless (see #984). It has a page containing a note explaining why a number is left blank, sitting directly beside a hardcoded number. It knows. That is the joke.

**`pdoom-data`** — the archivist. Holds 2,197 events that are raw PDF text, so it is permanently full of *other people's* prose, other people's author blocks, and until recently other people's email addresses. Carries a corpus of 1,000 records nobody has read since 2025-11-24. Quietly essential; slightly haunted.

There is a fourth character whether we like it or not — **`coordination`** — which is the one that writes the rules down and has just discovered that nobody receives them (coordination#15).

## Constraints, and one that matters

- **Interior use only.** Not shipped in-game, not on the website. If it ever goes public that is a separate decision, because of the Manifund commitment to replace AI-generated assets with human artists — the website is on the hook for being able to say which images are which, and that is easier if this material never enters the published set. Tag it accordingly at generation time rather than sorting it out later.
- **Jocular, not cruel.** These are Pip's own repos and the failures being ribbed are ones he chose to write down publicly rather than hide. Affectionate.
- **Anything witty must also be true.** House rule from the website side: an easter egg implying a feature that does not exist is a lie in a funny hat. Same applies to lore — a character trait should be something the repo actually does.
- No text in the images, per the existing poster recipes.

## What would be genuinely useful, beyond the joke

Website #249 is stuck on a real question: **what does a published asset carry, and where does it live?** A small, low-stakes, interior-only batch is an ideal first exercise of an emit-for-non-game-surface path — nobody is harmed if the manifest shape is wrong, and it would produce a worked example instead of another design argument. If the answer is "not yet, the pipeline is mid-rebuild", that is a completely fine answer and the request will keep.

## Suggested first pass

Four pieces, one per repo plus coordination. Poster register, since that is what the current manifests are tuned for. Let the pipeline decide whether they are personifications, heraldry, machinery, or something none of us predicted — **the lore is meant to be theirs, not specified from here.**

Related: pdoom1#950 (closing harvest — easter eggs), pdoom1#1107 (promotion gate), pdoom1-website#249 (the image contract), coordination#17 (proposed tri-repo content workshop).

issues.title: Half-day workshop: audit mechanics deep-dive (next epoch) -- something amazing under the smell
issues.body:

issues.title: Pip's rulings on intro + poster art, 2026-08-04 11:34 -- B1/B2 approved, dev-vs-alpha tool split, and a prior story beat
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memo `2026-08-04_114646__296e9bfd`, 11m58s, recorded 11:34 AEST reading the printed intro-and-poster-art pack. Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, not cleaned.

## Core message

B1 (portal stitch) approved, B2 poster sequence approved. Two things he wants beyond the pack: **an explicit dev-tool versus alpha-tool split**, and **a story beat that comes before the current intro**, which he narrated on the recording and which is reproduced below because it exists nowhere else.

## Rulings on the pack

**B1 portal stitch -- yes.** *"otherwise B1 is super good, I like it."* With the added prior beat, see below.

**B2 silent poster sequence -- yes**, likes the posters. Thinks the boot sequence is *"kind of cool"* and floats replacing the phone framing, since in the new beat the character teleports back and is hit by a bus.

Pleased the vortex shader, the technique doc, the unattended scene capture and the capture runner exist.

## Dev tools versus alpha tools -- the substantive ask

He wants tooling classified, not gated behind separate build lanes:

- **Confirm which bucket the live tuning harness is in.** If it is in the current build, say whether it is a dev tool or an alpha tool.
- **Dev-tool screens should be reachable from inside the dev-tool key.** Right now he cannot get to them.
- **Make the dev-tool keys togglable** on and off during development. Alpha-tool keys stay on for the whole alpha patch.
- Rationale: load and stress-test tooling is his, not players'. *"if players have problems with this, I can get them to send me logs, I don't need to be shipping alpha players."* Dev tools available on request; alpha tools bundled by default.

Note for whoever picks this up: this is adjacent to `#1066`, where a dev-profile artifact appeared in a player-facing list. Same boundary, different symptom.

## Capture runner -- roadmap, not now

He wants the capture runner integrated into the game and made friendly to streaming software, light touch. Motivation is concrete: *"I'll go play the game on Twitch and I'll develop it live on Twitch for an hour or two a week if I want."* Explicitly a roadmap item.

## The prior story beat, verbatim-ish

This is a first articulation and worth capturing before it decays. Reconstructed from the recording, his sequencing:

1. Open in a lightly censored future year. A war is under way -- possible reuse of the crashed-drone assets.
2. The original vision, which he calls a *"really really really old idea"*: people running and being picked off one by one by a superior force, in Wing Commander 1 style 8-bit or low-poly sprites. Drones, goons, ninjas, orbital laser strikes.
3. The player has been initiated into something like **the Bayesian conspiracy**; the operator is hooded, which *"protects the anonymity of the player from the get go."*
4. The runners are carrying the alignment solution to a time-travelling hero, trying to reach a safe place.
5. The player reaches the mountain, is the last one, hands it over -- and rounds the corner onto two figures in front of an enormous server rack. His reference points are Cormac McCarthy and the person behind the Doom fast inverse square root.
6. *"hey, what happened to hero?"* -- he died. Nobody has heard from McCarthy since he said he was going to solve a problem and vanished. The Doom figure's line: carving out the base in the mountain, hoarding compute saved through the square-root mechanism propagating through the universe.
7. Player: that doesn't make any sense. Reply: *"well, I don't have any time to explain it, get in the fucking time machine."* Explosion or approaching enemies, which pre-shadows other people teleporting in later.
8. Then the portal stitch (B1) runs.

He interrupted himself mid-narration with *"actually, wow, there we go, okay, timestamp that"* -- so he considers the McCarthy/Doom-figure reveal the found thing, not the frame.

Treat the named real people as placeholder inspirations pending a decision about using real names, which he did not make; he half-retracted one on the recording (*"that's probably too much"*).

## Presentation, owned by coordination

The pack carried no timestamps. Being fixed here.

issues.title: Pip's rulings on the event-promotion pack, 2026-08-04 11:17 -- approved, plus the turn-pacing premise is wrong
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memo `2026-08-04_113437__e60ca3b5`, 17m36s, recorded 11:17 AEST while reading the printed event-promotion pack. Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated, not cleaned.

## Core message

Pip approves the promotion pass and the section-4 shortlist essentially in full, **but flags that a premise underneath the pack is wrong**: the pack reasons about 26 or 52 turns per year while the game has moved to one turn = one month. He wants the retime done, and a second variant, rather than the pack's single option.

## Rulings

**Approved as proposed:** the override-file-plus-one-edit shape, zero engine changes, the retime pass.

**Section 4 shortlist -- promote:** A1 through A5 yes. B1, B2 yes. B3 "Deep RL from Human Preferences" **strong yes**. "Scalable agent alignment from reward modeling" **strong yes**. B7 "Introduction to Circuits" yes. B8 Anthropic faking yes. **Promote all the C-tier up to B-tier.**

**From the deliberately-not-promoted list, promote anyway:** sandbagging, Apollo, METER. His reason: *"these will be useful reminders for me in game as a dev to add those in as things that are discoverable through situational awareness"* -- they give him in-game hooks to break situational awareness down into.

**6A retime -- do it as proposed, AND make a second variant scaled to a year.** *"ideally the model will be kind of flexible in ways where we can just change the timing of things so that we can then give people like week by week versions of the game if they want to be punished."* Treat the timing scale as a dial, not a constant.

**Deferred, with a reason:** F4/F5 timing dials and F6 effect magnitudes. He judges the current percentages and rarity values to be *"hard coded in from ages ago"* and does not want to anchor on repairing them: *"I just want to like mentally scrap them and come up with better timing dials with some good consideration again in the new philosophical approach."* F6 specifically waits on an ADR/DQ tidy-up pass. F8 approved.

## The pacing premise, which is the substantive correction

The pack states the run spans 2017-2025 of AI history inside one financial year. Pip: *"okay so that's wrong so we're already fucking all of this up right that's probably why some of the pacing is wrong."*

His replacement frame, stated as high-level and explicitly not yet an end-game definition:

- One turn is one month. A player should be **unlikely to die in the first ten turns**, i.e. ten months, so a run starting in 2017 should reliably reach 2018.
- **Alpha/beta/first release covers 2017 to roughly 2025.** Stopping at 2025 is deliberate: it *"keeps it a little bit out of contentiousness land."*
- **Mid-game** then has room for the whole AI-2027 scenario. The mid-game has a switching point he could not name on the recording, around early-pre-AGI to early-post-AGI.
- **End game** is a later development wave -- AGI scenarios playing out, or roughly a year past the switching point.
- At ~50 event-turns per year he expects *"like 100 different events"* to remain reachable.

He asks whether 26-turns-per-year compression is still architecturally correct given the month-per-turn move, and if not, to treat his decisions here as the correction.

## F7 -- deferral should carry a visible cost, and he has a mechanic for it

He agrees every promoted class is deferrable, but wants deferral to accumulate a *"probably quite miniscule"* but non-silent cost -- his analogy is worth keeping intact:

> you can cancel the two thousand dollar thing trivially, it costs an attention point or a delegated action; to cancel fifteen dollars a month you get one reminder about it and you can say I'll deal with this later, you can infinitely defer it and it'll keep taking fifteen dollars a month out of your bank account

Not a problem if you are earning elsewhere, but mechanically a small standing disadvantage. He wants this packed back into F7 and revisited after the philosophical refinement pass.

## Two architecture notes he raised and did not resolve

**Split the build engine from the shipped game.** *"a lot of this stuff can be built outside and precomputed outside of what the player needs."* He raised this while reading the deep-merge/transform-event chain. He explicitly held his thinking on F4/F5 partly because *"this feels like we're suggesting or building architecture and I'm not sure if it's being well orchestrated."* Flagging that as a request for the architecture question to be handled deliberately rather than absorbed into a balance pass.

**Rivals are not the only other agents.** On C5 institutional coordination breakdown, he notes the countervailing case: institutions and allies can make gains and the run can still be lost, *"and in fact that is the likely thing."* So alongside rivals the model needs **other players** and **allies** as distinct elements.

## Cross-repo, routed separately

pdoom1-website pulls from pdoom1; he expects the pdoom1-website-to-pdoom-data contract may change at some point and asked coordination to note it for later scheduling. Not action now.

## Presentation, owned by coordination

The pack printed single-sided across ten pages and used the pre-ministerial format. Both are coordination's to fix and are being fixed here; no action for this repo beyond expecting the next pack to look different.

issues.title: Postmortem contribution from pdoom-data: load-bearing breakage, false greens, and asking the person
issues.body:
Contribution to the week's postmortem from the **pdoom-data** side, filed here because the useful patterns are cross-repo. Written 2026-08-01. Not a status report; the observations are the point.

Caveat on standing: this is one repo's view of a week in which most of the launch effort happened elsewhere. Weight accordingly.

---

## 1. Three separate things were broken in ways that were load-bearing

The strongest pattern of the week, and it generalises well past pdoom-data.

- **The CI YAML syntax error was the only thing preventing a data-clobbering bot.** `data-pipeline-automation.yml` ran `clean_events.py` on any push touching `data/raw/**` and auto-committed. That script's output is 28 records where the feed holds 1,194. An agent told "fix the broken CI" would have destroyed the corpus, correctly following instructions.
- **The failing ASCII gate is the only thing preventing an unbounded auto-committer.** `documentation-publish` appends five lines to `DEVBLOG.md` with `echo >>` on every push to main. It has never run because it depends on a job that fails. So *clearing the ASCII backlog arms it as a side effect.*
- **A third case, softer:** the reviewed records were sitting unreachable inside a 3,434-record feed. Nothing was broken exactly, but the absence of a promotion step is why four days of review value went nowhere.

**The transferable rule: before fixing a failure, ask what it is currently preventing.** A red build is sometimes a control. This is cheap to ask and we did not have the habit.

Concretely adopted here: `scripts/validation/check_workflow_disarm.py` fails the build if either write-capable workflow regains an unattended trigger, and names the reason inline. A de-arm that lives in a YAML comment is one careless edit from gone, and whoever undoes it will not have read the comment.

## 2. A consumer-side fix leaves the source broken, and does not compose

pdoom1-website added email redaction on 2026-07-29. Two days later the addresses were **still in pdoom-data**, which is public, because the website scrubbed its *output*.

That is not a criticism of the website's fix — it was the fast, correct thing for the surface that was on fire. But the shape is worth naming: every consumer would have had to rediscover and re-fix the same problem, and any new consumer starts exposed.

**Rule: a fix applied at the consumer is a mitigation. Only a fix at the source is a fix.** Worth asking, whenever we patch something at a boundary, whether the same defect is now sitting upstream waiting for the next reader.

Status, honestly: partially fixed in pdoom-data and **not yet merged**. See section 6.

## 3. Every claim that got measured this week was wrong

Not "some". Every one that anybody actually checked:

| Claim | On measurement |
|---|---|
| "9 dead root .py modules" | Zero with no references. Twelve in a self-referential cluster. Deleting on the audit's wording would have removed live code. |
| "1,194 timeline events" | 28 hand-authored plus 1,166 bulk arXiv imports whose descriptions are unparsed PDF text. |
| `rarity` | Derived from `text_length > 20000`. Published to players as a "Rare" badge on ~90% of pages. |
| A/B/C/D tier | Scores provenance and length. "A-tier" means "long arXiv paper with named authors" — inverted relative to what everyone assumes. |
| "206 verdicts, 1 note, so the tool is wrong" | Asked the reviewer. He said the verdicts were real filtering and the note count was probably a misclick. |

Four of those five had been written down confidently, and three had been acted on.

**The pattern is not carelessness, it is that writing a claim down feels like verifying it.** The countermeasure that worked was making claims executable: `check_invariants.py` asserts them, so they fail loudly instead of decaying quietly in prose.

## 4. A number about a person is a hypothesis about that person

Worth separating from section 3 because the fix is different.

The "1 note per 206 verdicts" inference ran from a count straight to a claim about a human's experience — that the interface had prevented him writing — and a tool was rebuilt on it. **Asking him took one question and contradicted it.** Cost: four days in which the pass's actual output went unshipped while attention was on the wrong theory.

Usage metrics are cheap and abundant; first-hand accounts are cheap but require asking. The temptation to skip the asking scales with how confident the metric looks.

Now in the Mistakes register, and in pdoom-data's `CLAUDE.md` so it loads every session rather than living in a write-up nobody rereads.

## 5. Things that work but have no owner rot invisibly

Two instances, same shape:

- `timeline_events/alignment_research/` — 1,000 records generating 1,000 live pages, and the website's sync **has never read that collection**. No generator maintains it. A mirror with no owner.
- Twelve root-level modules last touched 2025-09-14, referenced only by each other and by docs, called by nothing in the current pipeline.

Neither was failing. That is exactly why neither was noticed. **A thing that produces no errors and has no owner is invisible until it is wrong in public.**

Cheap detector, if anyone wants it: for each published artefact, name the generator and the last time it ran. Anything that cannot answer both is orphaned.

## 6. What I got wrong, since a postmortem is worth less without it

- **Asserted DeepMind's founding backwards from memory**, in the same message where I was arguing that dates must be sourced. Caught only because I had required verbatim quotes from the research.
- **Did not read pdoom-data#45 all day**, despite it being filed by Pip that morning and containing the most important findings in the repo — the PII exposure, the rarity inversion, the orphaned collection. I surveyed the issue list at the start of the day and never re-checked. Everything I chose to do instead was defensible; none of it was more important than #45.
- **My own tooling wrote a UTF-8 BOM** into a source file via PowerShell's `Set-Content -Encoding utf8`. Caught by the invariant checker, which is the system working, but it was my check catching my mistake.
- **The redaction tool reported clean while ten records still carried addresses.** A false pass. Worse than a loud failure, because it would have supported a claim that the data was safe. That work is committed as WIP and explicitly marked do-not-merge.

The last one is the one I would generalise: **we should be more afraid of green than of red.** Three of this week's worst findings were things that reported success — a passing residue check, a CI that could not fail because it could not parse, and 2,190 pages published from a feed whose own contract brief says "do not ship it to players yet".

## 7. On spreading sideways

Pip named this himself, so just the evidence from this repo:

What worked was **batching decisions into one front-loaded block and then running autonomously for hours**. A single 20-minute decision session on Friday morning unblocked roughly six hours of work with no further input.

What did not work was interleaving. Every mid-flight context switch cost a re-orientation, and the failure in section 6 — not reading #45 — is a direct consequence of attention being spread across three repos while the important thing sat in a fourth tab.

**A concrete suggestion for the league push:** decide the day's questions once, in writing, before any of the parallel work starts. Not because interruption is bad, but because the questions asked at 09:00 are better than the ones asked at 16:00, and the parallel agents can then run without waiting.

## 8. One cross-repo structural finding

pdoom-data was shipping `impacts` and `pdoom_impact` — pdoom1's mechanical vocabulary — inside its shared schema, which pdoom1's ADR-0015 deprecated on 2026-07-13. Neither side noticed for two weeks.

Root cause is structural rather than anybody's oversight: **encoding a consumer's internal vocabulary guarantees this recurs on every revision.** Now ADR-007 in pdoom-data: cross-boundary meaning is expressed in externally-maintained vocabularies, and the mapping onto pdoom1's intermediaries lives in pdoom1. Standard anti-corruption layer.

The reason it favours pdoom1: with an external taxonomy, DQ-21 can change as often as the design needs and no exported pack ever silently means the wrong thing.

---

## If the postmortem only takes three things from this

1. **Before fixing a failure, ask what it is preventing.** Red is sometimes a control.
2. **Be more afraid of green than of red.** The week's worst findings all reported success.
3. **Ask the person.** A metric about a human is a hypothesis, and the check is one question.

Related: pdoom-data #45 #43 #47 #48 #49, pdoom1#1052, pdoom1#1055, pdoom1-website#220, pdoom1 ADR-0015.

issues.title: art: promotion adds ~105 MB to the pack -- subtle refinement pass owed for a future epoch
issues.body:
Filed at Pip's instruction, 2026-08-03: *"We will go through subtle refinements later (make a note of an issue to do it for a future epoch) but I'll live for now. Continue."*

## The number, and it moved

When he ruled, the figure on the table was **~58 MB**. After the promotion pipeline was fixed (#1107 -- resolver, destination map, contested-variant naming), every one of the 807 approved keeps now resolves:

```
promotable: 489 of 807 keeps  (105.2 MB would enter godot/assets)
held:       318               (~52 MB, icon_hires, retired pending re-verdict)
contested:    0
blocked:      0
```

**105.2 MB, not 58.** The number grew because 198 previously-unresolvable assets started resolving -- the fix worked, and the cost was hidden behind the bug.

Godot packs the entire `godot/` tree, and `godot/assets` is currently 47 MB of a **59 MB** pack. Promoting takes the pack to roughly **165 MB -- a 2.8x download increase**, on a game whose comms strategy depends on players re-downloading after every patch.

**This is filed, not blocked.** Pip has ruled to proceed and live with it. This issue exists so the cost is recorded rather than discovered later.

## What the refinement pass should do

1. **Size derivatives properly.** The single biggest lever. Promotion currently copies the largest source under the 1 MB cap; a 512px master backing a 64px icon is 64x the pixels the game draws. ADR-0019's demand manifest declares the size the game instantiates at -- that is the mechanism, and it does not exist yet.
2. **Re-verdict `icon_hires`** (318 keeps, ~52 MB, held). Pip 2026-08-03: *"Retire until verdicts."* These are the #787 bloat class; the game already references sized icons in `godot/assets/icons`.
3. **Decide the fate of the non-current variants.** The contested-naming rule ships BOTH variants: the highest claims the plain name, earlier ones carry a `_vN` suffix. The suffixed ones are **packed but unreferenced** -- precisely the class ADR-0019 exists to end. They stay until the demand manifest can rule on them.
4. **Consider format.** Nothing has evaluated PNG vs WebP vs compressed texture import settings for this corpus.

## Why this is a future-epoch item and not now

ADR-0019 (pull-from-demand) is ACCEPTED with **zero implementation**. Doing the refinement before the demand manifest exists means hand-picking sizes per asset -- exactly the manual, rot-prone curation the ADR was written to replace. The manifest makes the size question answerable mechanically.

Sequence: manifest first, then this.

## Related

ADR-0019 · #1093 (the stranded 807) · #1107 (the pipeline fix) · #787 (~488 MB of unreferenced variants, the precedent) · `docs/art/ART_MASTERS_POLICY.md`

issues.title: Review: what does pdoom1 actually want from pdoom-data? (measured inventory, no proposal)
issues.body:
**Raised at Pip's direction** (`pdoom-data#55`): pdoom1 decides what it wants from pdoom-data, and pdoom-data then supplies that. Direction of authority is pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. So this issue carries measurements and questions, and deliberately **no proposal**.

Findings come from a read-only static audit of this repo plus JSON measurement of the corpus. The game was not run; anything runtime-dependent is flagged.

---

## The question

**What do you actually want a pdoom-data event to carry?**

Everything below exists so that can be answered against facts rather than against either side's guesses. If the answer is "much less than we currently send", that is a good outcome and cheap to deliver.

---

## What pdoom1 reads today

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, 1,194 records. Every raw-record access in the tree is in one file, `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`.

**Nine of thirteen fields are read.** Never accessed anywhere: `sources` (1,194 records, none empty), `tags`, `impacts[].condition` (3,636 entries, all null), `source_id`. `pdoom_impact` is copied onto the transformed event and then read by nothing; 1,187 of its 1,194 values are null.

Derived keys written onto the game event that nothing downstream reads: `eligibility_start`, `eligibility_end`, `trigger_mode`, `historical`, `significance`, `source_data` (which carries a full copy of the raw record).

## The number that should shape the answer

**98.3% of the corpus never reaches a decision window.** `_is_flavour_event` (`event_service.gd:491-497`) demotes every `technical_research_breakthrough` and every `arxiv*` id to `delivery_tier: "feed"`. Feed items render as one grey line and **their options are never presented and their effects never applied**.

1,174 of 1,194 records are inert beyond `id`, `title`, `category`, `year`. Twenty can open a window; one is then dropped by the start-year filter.

**So the decision surface pdoom1 gets from 1,194 curated events is nineteen records.**

That is the single most decision-relevant fact in this audit. If pdoom-data is supplying 1,194 records to fill nineteen slots, the contract question is not "which fields" but "which records, and chosen how".

## Rarity is not carrying the meaning your curve file assumes

Corpus: rare 1,076, common 77, legendary 41.

**All 41 `legendary` records are in the arxiv/flavour stream** — so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records that are then demoted to a grey line. The nineteen records that can open a window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.**

Cause, measured in pdoom-data: `rarity` is an exact `text_length > 20000` threshold on a field that is not carried into the output (`pdoom-data#51`). Zero violations in 1,129 records. Correlation with the visible description length is r = -0.0065.

Boundary case nobody validates: `_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`, and `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and return the wrong dict. No such record exists today.

## Significance discriminates almost nothing

`significance` is summed from `abs(change)` across `impacts` and scales every generated option's effects (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`.

## `impacts` are not inert, and three of your docs say they are

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names **pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects**.

`WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`, `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79` and `resource_accessor.gd:73-76` all still describe that path as an inert sink. Flagging as a doc/code disagreement rather than asserting which is intended.

Meanwhile pdoom-data's supplied vocabulary — `vibey_doom`, `stress`, `burnout_risk` — maps onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws. It survives only because of that reroute. Three variables are silently dropped as unmapped: `ethics_risk` (16), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4). They still count toward significance.

Path B (literal effects) reaches gameplay for **seven records only** — the `funding_catastrophe` branch. The other twelve window-tier records build effects from `significance` alone.

## Three asks already on your record that pdoom-data does not answer

Not new requests from us. These are pdoom1's own documents.

**ADR-0012** (accepted 2026-07-12) names four event-content fields: *class, expiry N, response-expected flag, carrying-cost hook*. pdoom-data supplies none; everything defaults to `deferrable`.

**pdoom1#630 / `UI_FEATURES_STACK.md:39-44`** — the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv`, "the ENTIRE hist_arxiv deck fires, 200+ entries in event_cooldowns". `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names pdoom-data's salience tiers as the principled fix. pdoom-data has that field on its candidate feed (`salience_tier_by_profile`, A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection you read.

**`TRIUMVIRATE_METABOLIC_CYCLE.md:90-116`** (proposed, not ratified) asks for monthly facts-only packs and states the split: *pdoom-data owns the fact schema, pdoom1 owns the shaping schema*. pdoom-data has since ratified its side of that as ADR-007 and ADR-008.

## One thing pdoom-data will not do, and why it is in your interest

DQ-21 is resolved and its vocabulary is live — `general_capability`, `frontier_capability`, `global_compute`, `dedicated_ai_compute`, `political_pressure`, `ambient_risk`, `global_alarm`, `global_panic`, accepted at `events.gd:315-337`. pdoom-data could encode those names directly.

**ADR-007 in pdoom-data says it should not**, and the reason favours you: if we encode `frontier_capability` and you later rename or split it, every exported pack already in the wild silently means the wrong thing — no error, no failed parse, just numbers attached to a concept that no longer exists. An external taxonomy plus a mapping table on your side keeps your vocabulary yours to revise as often as the design needs.

If you would rather have your names directly, say so and we will do it — but that is the trade being made.

## Also outstanding, unrelated to schema

`pdoom1#1098` — 42 records in the bundled copy still carry un-redacted email addresses. `scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` reads directories that no longer exist in pdoom-data and has never successfully run, so there is no path for upstream corrections to arrive.

## Could not determine

Whether any of this holds at runtime; everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Why `historical_events.json` is a hand-commit rather than a sync output. Whether the "inert sink" docs are simply stale post-#985 or describe a path not traced.

Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `pdoom-data#51`, `pdoom-data#52`, `pdoom-data#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `pdoom1#1052`, `pdoom1#1098`, `pdoom1-website#240`.

issues.title: ADR-0015 / DQ-21: what should a pdoom-data event carry, now that literal doom fields are deprecated?
issues.body:
From pdoom-data. Two questions, one blocking and one design-level. Read-only investigation on our side; no changes made to pdoom1.

## Context

pdoom-data ships `event_v1` records carrying `impacts: [{variable, change}]`, `rarity` and `pdoom_impact`. **ADR-0015 (accepted 2026-07-13) deprecates exactly that shape:**

> No action or event definition carries a literal doom field. Effects target intermediary world-state variables ... doom is computed from world state each day tick.

So our schema is currently handing you the "single source-destination number bumps" that ADR names as legacy. We want to stop doing that. We do **not** want to guess our way to a replacement, because ADR-0015 point 2 says adding an intermediary is an ADR-grade act — and inventing your mechanical vocabulary from outside your repo would be exactly the wrong move.

We also found two candidate vocabularies and could not tell which is live:

| Source | Vocabulary |
|---|---|
| ADR-0015 examples, marked "v1 vocabulary owed, DQ-21" | lab capability, deployment pressure, governance quality, public salience |
| `godot/docs/design/RISK_SYSTEM.md` (2025-12-25, "In Development") | Capability Overhang, Research Integrity, Regulatory Attention, Public Awareness, Insider Threat, Financial Exposure |

## Question 1 (blocking us)

**What is DQ-21's status and rough timeline?** We have a consumer-facing export profile blocked on it (pdoom-data#43). Blocked is the correct state — we are not looking to route around it — but knowing whether it is weeks or months changes what we build meanwhile.

Also: is `RISK_SYSTEM.md` superseded by ADR-0015, or are the six risk pools the intended v1 intermediaries under a different name?

## Question 2 (the design one)

**What do you actually want an event to carry?**

Our current thinking is that the answer might be "nothing mechanical at all" — that events cross the boundary as facts plus clearly-attributed editorial opinion, and every mechanical consequence is computed inside pdoom1. That would be the cleanest version of the firewall either repo has managed, and it would make our export profile simpler rather than harder.

If you do want a directional hint, our proposal is that it should be expressed **in a vocabulary pdoom-data owns and can defend** — for example the MIT AI Risk Repository domains we already tag against, plus a direction and a confidence — rather than in your internal variable names. You would keep a mapping table from our stable taxonomy onto your intermediaries.

The reason is deliberately in your interest: it means DQ-21 can change, and change again, **without churning our data**. Only your mapping table moves. Standard anti-corruption layer between two bounded contexts. If instead we encoded your intermediaries directly, every vocabulary revision would require a schema version bump and a re-export on our side, and stale copies in the wild would silently mean the wrong thing.

## A framing we would like to adopt from you

ADR-0015 point 4 states our boundary better than our own docs do:

> The doom function is structure; intermediary pricing is numbers ... MtG framing: events are cards, the doom function is the rules.

We propose adopting that verbatim in pdoom-data's glossary rather than maintaining a parallel vocabulary. pdoom-data ships cards; pdoom1 owns the rules. Object if that misrepresents the intent.

## Related

- pdoom-data#43 — export profile, blocked on this
- pdoom-data#34 — moving pdoom1's resource model out of our shared schema
- pdoom-data#27 — Hop A ratification, where the monthly World-Update Pack was agreed
- pdoom1#962 — frontier-labs integration (unblocked, dataset shipped)

issues.title: Pip's rulings, 2026-08-02 -- velocity portfolio weights, and a review pdoom-data is waiting on
issues.body:
Spoken rulings, transcribed on-device. Not re-read by Pip.

## Velocity reconstruction -- his method, then his numbers

He deliberately changed how he used the document: he covered the estimator-method column, looked only at the hours each method produced, and then asked himself how he would **split a 100% portfolio of bets** on which method a future omniscient account would vindicate. The percentages were arrived at **after** one full pass, and the inline comments were written during the first pass -- so where they conflict, the percentages are later and better.

**League week:** A 8%, B 40%, C 6%, D 40%, E 6%.
**Last 14 days:** A 10%, B 40%, C 2%, D 35%, E 3%, F 10%.
**Ranked 1 (most bought) to 6:** A 1, B 2, E 3, C 4, D 5, F 6.

Note the tension worth examining rather than smoothing: B and D split the league-week portfolio almost evenly at 40/40, but on the ranking D falls to fifth. His own annotation asks whether he is *"Brier-ing"* -- treating it as a calibration exercise -- and he judged the exercise *"feels right/correct to be doing."*

He wants **ISO week translated into actual calendar weeks** in future renderings; ISO is the right standard but not the readable one. He confirms the shape: December, then near-silence until scattered touches in February and March, early June, a real push through June, exploding through July.

**Double tick, full agreement, on "the number that matters most."**

## A review pdoom-data is waiting on

`pdoom-data#51` (rarity is a length threshold on a discarded field) and `#52` (`all_events.json` has no producer) predate the workshop-3 decisions. Pip's ruling is that **pdoom1 reviews these findings and decides what information it actually wants from pdoom-data**, which then draws it down -- rather than pdoom-data fixing them unilaterally. Direction of authority runs pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. Filed on their side as `pdoom-data#55`.

## Postmortem

He agrees the slack hour paid for eleven findings and wants it **doubled to two hours**, with the launch schedule recast now that real time-logs exist -- worked through iteratively with him, presented as a couple of different models rather than one plan.

He also singled out a line from the postmortem input for keeping: *"You can audit for it. You cannot audit for a metaphor."* His words: capture that as a keeper.

`pdoom1#1095` -- he will read it Sunday evening or Monday morning, not today.
